seoTitle: The Mentalist Test: Which Character Are You? (12 Questions)
metaDescription: Take The Mentalist test: 12 everyday questions reveal whether you're Patrick Jane, Teresa Lisbon, Cho, Rigsby, Van Pelt, Wylie — or Red John. Get your full character breakdown.
intro: Are you the one who reads everyone in the room, the one holding the whole team together, or the one quietly pulling the strings? Answer 12 questions about how you really handle people, rules and pressure and find out which Mentalist character you are, with a full percentage breakdown.

characters.name: Patrick Jane
characters.title: The Charming Mind-Reader
characters.summary: You notice everything, you say the thing nobody else would, and you get away with it because you're impossible to stay mad at.
description: Like Jane, you read people the way other people read menus. He made a living as a fake TV psychic before he joined the CBI — and he can still tell what you had for breakfast from the way you're standing.

You're playful on the surface: the naps on the office couch, the hiding place in the attic, the perfectly brewed cup of tea. Underneath, there's one thing you care about so much you'd rearrange your whole life around it — for Jane, it was the man who took his family.

Rules feel optional to you. You'd rather apologise afterwards than ask permission first. And when it all goes wrong, you're the type to vanish to an island and write letters to the one person you can't stop thinking about.
characters.flaw: You bend every rule, and the people who love you end up cleaning up the mess.
characters.signature: A cup of tea, a comfy couch and a smug little smile when the suspect finally cracks.
characters.clashReason: they can see right through you — and they'll say it out loud

characters.name: Teresa Lisbon
characters.title: The One Who Holds It All Together
characters.summary: You're the responsible one. You lead, you protect your people, and you quietly carry more than anyone realises.
description: Like Lisbon, you grew up fast. She lost her mother young and helped raise her brothers — and that sense of responsibility never left. You're the one everyone calls when something goes wrong.

You believe in doing things properly: procedure, evidence, a case that holds up in court. But you'll back someone you trust even when they're driving you up the wall. Lisbon covered for Jane again and again.
You don't stop serving, whatever happens. When the CBI was shut down, Lisbon became police chief of a small town in Washington — and then Jane got on a plane to tell her how he felt.
characters.flaw: You take on everyone's problems and never let anyone take care of you.
characters.signature: Badge on the belt, a small cross at her neck, and a look that says "Jane, what did you do?"
characters.clashReason: they'd make you follow the rules you've been ignoring

characters.name: Kimball Cho
characters.title: The Unreadable Professional
characters.summary: Few words, zero drama, total reliability. People can't read you — and you like it that way.
description: Like Cho, you don't waste words. While everyone else panics, you've done the job, written it up and gone back to your paperback.
You've come a long way. Cho ran with a street gang as a teenager before the army straightened him out — and he's been the steadiest person in every room since.
You handle pain alone, sometimes too alone. When Cho was hurt on the job, he hid how badly — right up until it nearly cost a teammate. Then he fixed it himself, quietly.
characters.flaw: People have no idea what you're feeling — sometimes, neither do you.
characters.signature: A plain black jacket, a novel on the desk and a one-word answer that ends the conversation.
characters.clashReason: they'd find your drama exhausting and wouldn't pretend otherwise

characters.name: Wayne Rigsby
characters.title: The Big-Hearted Protector
characters.summary: Loyal, warm and always a little bit hungry. You wear your heart on your sleeve and you'd go to war for the people you love.
description: Like Rigsby, you're the heart of the group. You'll crack the joke that breaks the tension, eat the last snack in the break room, then put yourself between your friends and danger without thinking twice.
You're not defined by where you came from. Rigsby's father was a biker with a violent past, and Rigsby chose to be the opposite: a cop, a husband and a devoted dad.
You feel things big. Rigsby broke the CBI's rules for Grace Van Pelt, married her, and eventually left the job to build a life with her.
characters.flaw: Your temper and your stomach both make decisions before your brain does.
characters.signature: A sandwich in one hand, his badge in the other, and a hopeful look at whatever the suspect is cooking.
characters.clashReason: they'd say exactly what they think, then eat your lunch

characters.name: Grace Van Pelt
characters.title: The Idealist With Steel Inside
characters.summary: You believe the best in people and you're open to the world — but underestimate you once and you'll never do it again.
description: Like Van Pelt, you're open to the world. Early on she was the one member of the team who believed some psychics might be real — and she wasn't afraid to argue with Jane about it.
You're tougher than you look. When Van Pelt discovered that her fiancé was working for Red John, she didn't fall apart. She did what had to be done.
You're sharp with the tech side of the job — computers were Van Pelt's speciality — and you want a life beyond work too. She and Rigsby left to start their own business together.
characters.flaw: You give your trust too quickly, and it's cost you before.
characters.signature: Headphones on, three screens open, and the surprise that she's the best shot in the room.
characters.clashReason: they'd believe things you'd never buy

characters.name: Jason Wylie
characters.title: The Sweet Tech Genius
characters.summary: Quiet, kind and secretly brilliant. You're the one who actually finds the answer — then gets flustered when anyone notices.
description: Like Wylie, you're happiest behind a screen, pulling phone records, tracing money and finding the one camera angle everyone else missed.
You're a little awkward and a lot kind. You'd rather help quietly than take credit loudly.
But part of you wants more than the desk. Wylie tried his hand at field work — not always gracefully — and proved he was braver than people assumed.
characters.flaw: You undersell yourself and wait too long to go after what you want.
characters.signature: Glasses, a hoodie, and the sentence "I think I found something."
characters.clashReason: they'd overthink everything you'd just do

characters.name: Red John
characters.title: The Puppet Master
characters.summary: Patient, controlled and always three steps ahead. You don't need the spotlight — you'd rather be the one pulling the strings.
description: Well. This is awkward. Like Red John, you understand people frighteningly well, and you know exactly what to say to make them trust you.

You're patient. You'd rather wait years for the perfect moment than act too early, and you enjoy being underestimated — Red John hid in plain sight for a decade, with loyal followers planted everywhere.
Relax: in real life this just means you're strategic, observant and very hard to fool. Probably.
characters.flaw: You need to be the smartest person in every room — and you hate being outplayed.
characters.signature: A smiley face, painted in red.
characters.clashReason: they'd play games with your mind

questions.text: Your friend brings their new partner to dinner. What are you quietly working out?

options.text: What they're not saying — it's all in their body language
Whether they can be trusted with your friend
Whether they're going to finish that plate
What they want — and whether you could use it

questions.text: Your boss gives you a rule you think is pointless. You...

options.text: Ignore it and do it your way. Results are what count
Follow it — but argue to get it changed
Do what you're told. Arguing isn't worth the stress
Smile and agree — then quietly work around it

questions.text: Someone hurts a person you love. What happens next?

options.text: You'll make it right, however many years it takes
You make sure they face real consequences — properly, so it sticks
Honestly? You want to punch them
Do whatever it takes to stop them

questions.text: A friend asks how you're really doing after a terrible week. You say...

options.text: "Fine." And that's the end of it
Everything — ideally over a big plate of food
The truth. You're an open book, for better or worse
"I'm okay. How are you doing?"

questions.text: You've developed feelings for someone you work with. You...

options.text: Go for it, even if it gets complicated
Keep it strictly professional. For years
Push it aside. Work comes first
Overthink it for months, then say something awkward
Read a book in total silence. Do not disturb
Eat. Nap. Eat again
Something spiritual — yoga, a retreat, a tarot reading
Visit an art gallery. Alone

questions.text: You pick up a new skill. It's...

options.text: Magic tricks. You love a good sleight of hand
Coding a game in your spare time
Martial arts. You won't say which belt
Running. Early, every day, no excuses

questions.text: Your team is in trouble with the people upstairs. You...

options.text: Stand up for them, even if it costs you
Quietly fix the problem that got you all in trouble
Keep your head down and let the work speak
Say nothing, and make sure you come out ahead either way

questions.text: A friend asks you to help work out whether their partner is lying to them. You...

options.text: Set a little trap: a question only a liar would get wrong
Tell them to just ask. Honesty first
Offer to have a word with the partner yourself if it turns out badly
Stay out of it. Not your relationship

questions.text: Snacks keep disappearing from your desk drawer. You...

options.text: Work out who it is by watching faces when you mention it
Leave a polite note and give them a chance to own up
Set up a tiny camera. Case closed by Friday
Keep quiet. It's probably you, eating them without noticing

questions.text: You're a detective. A woman has been murdered. Her husband has a solid alibi, but something about the way he talks about her feels off. Your boss says leave him alone. You...

options.text: Keep needling him until he slips up. You know he's lying
Back off officially, but keep checking quietly
Go through his phone and bank records for anything missed
Let him think he's off the hook. People get careless when they feel safe

questions.text: A child has gone missing. A famous TV psychic turns up offering to help, and the desperate parents believe every word. You...

options.text: Call them a fraud to their face. The parents deserve the truth
Let them talk, but keep them well away from the family
Hear them out. What if they really can see something?
Get to know the psychic. Someone that good at fooling people could be useful
